methodology.load_generator: 6 SEPARATE OS PROCESSES (scripts/loadgen_client.py), one keep-alive TCP connection each
methodology.application: real uvicorn server, 1 worker process(es), in its own OS process tree
methodology.database: PostgreSQL PostgreSQL 16.2 on x86_64-pc-mingw64, non-superuser role so FORCE row-level security is enforced
methodology.percentiles: computed over the merged per-request latencies from every worker, not averaged from per-worker percentiles
methodology.why_this_differs: The 624 ms SQLite and 995 ms PostgreSQL figures came from an in-process TestClient driven by N THREADS. That run's own breakdown showed only 22% of latency inside the database and a 20.3 ms mean on SELECT set_config(), a statement that touches no table and returns no rows -- i.e. it was measuring GIL contention between the generator and the handler. Separate processes remove that specific confound.
still_not_measured: one host, loopback TCP: no network latency, no load balancer, no ingress, no TLS termination
no competing tenants and no background workload

workload.rows_in_incidents_after: 0 -- suspicious: the run reported accepted writes. Check the tenant context above before believing this.
